decisions.reason: An address autocomplete web service runs on the firm's existing data infrastructure at near-zero marginal cost, so keeping this option open is cheap despite the lack of recent evidence.
An Austrian gas grid fee database needs ongoing data maintenance for a niche market, but it extends the firm's core energy-data offering and its value is still uncertain, so the option stays open.
Peak load window determination serves a regulatory need of German grid customers and is an algorithmic service that is cheap to maintain, so dropping it is not justified.
An end-customer tariff database is closely tied to the firm's core energy market data business and probably draws steady demand, so keeping it is warranted.
Custom web services are a flexible consulting offering with almost no fixed cost of keeping them on the market, so there is no reason to give up this option.
A postal code lookup service is a low-cost data product that complements the address and grid-fee services, so the option is cheap to keep.
